subject: OEM integration: co-engineering plan and timeline
messages:
From: Lina Park <lina.park@edgeware.ai>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: partners@edgeware.ai
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Exploring OEM embed — initial ask

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Edgeware is excited about embedding Redwood inference into our Agent Studio product. We did an internal scoping call this morning and want to propose a short co-engineering engagement to validate integration patterns and service-level assumptions before committing to a commercial OEM license.

High-level asks:
- A 4-week technical POC with a small dedicated engineering touchpoint from Redwood (API + deployment pattern).
- A simple SOW and a checklist of integration requirements (auth, telemetry, model selection, latency SLAs).
- A draft of suggested pricing/embedding terms so we can budget for Q4.

Can you share who on your side would own the co-engineering contact and a rough availability window in early August? We’re flexible on timing but prefer to start the POC in the first half of August.

Attaching our one-pager on Agent Studio for context.

Thanks,
Lina Park
Head of Partnerships — Edgeware AI
[attachment: AgentStudio-onepager.pdf (PDF, 220 KB)]

From: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
To: Lina Park <lina.park@edgeware.ai>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com, sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 11:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Exploring OEM embed — initial ask

Lina — really appreciate the clear asks and the one-pager. We’re definitely interested in a short co-engagement to surface integration risks. Quick notes from my side:

- We can run a 3–5 week technical POC. Typical scope: auth + network proof-of-concept, model selection & perf tests, and a deployment pattern (hosted vs dedicated) recommendation.
- Owner: Priyom Das (partnerships/product integration) will be the tech lead from Redwood; I’ll own project coordination and executive alignment.
- Availability: Priyom is available week of Aug 3 for kickoff.

Next steps I propose:
1) We circulate a short SOW (1–2 pages) capturing scope, success criteria, and roles.
2) Schedule a 30-min kickoff with Engineering + Security to confirm network requirements and sample workloads.
3) Share a one-sheet integration checklist and a draft commercial term card for OEM embedding.

I’m looping Priyom and Sergio here — Priyom, can you confirm capacity for early August and whether we want to bring on a solutions engineer for the first two weeks?

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: priyom.das@redwood.com
To: Lina Park <lina.park@edgeware.ai>, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 09:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Exploring OEM embed — initial ask

Hi Lina — thanks for the note and Hannah for the intro. I can own the tech lead role for this POC. Quick answers:

- Capacity: I can allocate 0.5 FTE for 4 weeks starting week of Aug 3. I’ll bring a solutions engineer (SE) for weeks 1–2 to accelerate onboarding and perf runs.
- What I’ll need from Edgeware for kickoff: a low-volume representative prompt set (10–20), a staging dataset for perf tests, and network diagrams (if you plan to access private instances).
- Deliverables: a short integration checklist, a deployment diagram, perf summary (latency/throughput), and recommended model/quantization profile.

I’ve attached a draft SOW and a preliminary integration checklist for review. Lina — please take a look and flag edits.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Principal Product Partnerships, Redwood Inference
[attachment: Edgeware_Redwood_OEM_SOW_v1.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)]

From: Victor Chen <v.chen@orbit-consult.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring OEM embed — initial ask

Hannah / Priyom — copying in Victor from Orbit Consulting; we’ll support Edgeware during the POC (network and enterprise procurement). A couple quick notes from the procurement side:

- Edgeware’s legal will want a standard OEM playbook: IP carveouts, data usage language (no persistent indexing of customer prompts), and clear termination criteria for the POC.
- For the POC, a short license letter + trial terms is acceptable; for production we’ll expect a commercial OEM agreement with committed usage tiers.

Victor — can you attach a sample OEM term sheet Edgeware prefers? We’ll align the SOW with that in the next revision.

—Victor Chen
Orbit Consulting (contracted by Edgeware)

From: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
To: Lina Park <lina.park@edgeware.ai>, priyom.das@redwood.com, sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 01 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Exploring OEM embed — initial ask

Thanks everyone — quick confirmation items after reviewing the draft SOW and checklist:

- Timeline: kickoff Tuesday Aug 4 at 10:00 AM ET (calendar invite sent).
- Resources: Priyom + SE confirmed; Sergio will join kickoff for commercial framing.
- Attachments: I uploaded a cleaned SOW (Edgeware_Redwood_OEM_SOW_v1.pdf), our redwood-integration-checklist.xlsx, and a deployment diagram to the partnership SharePoint. Links below.
- Legal/commercial: we’ll produce a short OEM term card post-POC once we have perf data. For the POC, Redwood will provide a limited-use trial license and audit logs during the engagement; Orbit/Edgeware — please send your preferred term sheet and we’ll map exceptions.

Action items before kickoff:
- Edgeware: share sample prompt set + any VPN/peering/network details (Victor/Edgeware).
- Redwood: circulate final SOW and a minimal test harness (curl-based) to validate auth tokens and sample requests.

Looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-integration-checklist.xlsx (XLSX, 45 KB)]
